title: All 6 ways to split 7, 9, 1, 3 into two pairs
caption: Each way of choosing which two values form group A gives a difference in means: −6, −2, 0, 0, 2 and 6, each as likely as the others under H₀. Only 1 of the 6 reaches 6, so the one-sided p = 1/6.
alt: Bar chart of the 6 permutations by difference in group means: −6 once, −2 once, 0 twice, 2 once and 6 once; the bar at 6 is highlighted.
description: There are C(4, 2) = 6 ways to choose group A.
Only one is at least as large as the observed 6: p = 1/6.
